newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban frees 31 Pakistani officials.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban frees 31 Pakistani officials.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia on Monday released all 31 men of Pakistan's Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) detained three days ago when they chased heroin smugglers across the border, officials said.
All the released personnel later arrived safely at Quetta, capital of the southwestern province of Baluchistan, provincial ANF chief Brigadier Mohammad Aslam told reporters.

Those detained were an army lietenant colonel who had led the team, a major, two captains and 27 soldiers who had crossed the border on Friday after a gun-battle with smugglers near the town of Chagai, about 35 km (22 miles) south of the frontier.
Their release followed hectic diplomatic and political efforts, Aslam said.
The smugglers had escaped after Friday's gun-battle, but the Pakistani force was captured by Taleban fighters who took them to the Afghan town of Lashkargarh, 10 km (six miles) inside the border.
Aslam said the Taleban had promised to return all weapons seized from the ANF team.
Team leader Javed Akhtar told reporters that the Taleban had treated his group well. "Their behaviour was good with us and we have not faced any kind of difficulty in their custody."
